content: Co-dydramol is a non-proprietary name that refers to a pharmaceutical preparation combining dihydrocodeine tartrate and paracetamol. This medication is formulated in tablet form and is primarily used for the management of moderate pain. Co-dydramol belongs to a broader category of combination drugs available in the UK and other countries. Examples of similar combination drugs include Co-codaprin (a combination of aspirin and codeine), Co-codamol (a combination of dihydrocodeine and paracetamol), and Co-proxamol (a combination of dextropropoxyphene and paracetamol). Each Co-dydramol tablet contains 5 mg of dihydrocodeine. Higher-strength formulations of this medication are classified as prescription-only medicines. For instance, the brand Paramol contains 46 mg of dihydrocodeine per tablet. There are different strengths of Co-dydramol available: Co-dydramol 10/500 contains 10 mg of dihydrocodeine and is the default preparation dispensed if no specific strength is indicated on a prescription. Co-dydramol 20/500 contains 20 mg of dihydrocodeine and is marketed under the branded name Remedeine. Co-dydramol 30/500 contains 30 mg of dihydrocodeine and is sold under the branded name Remedeine Forte. The naming convention for Co-dydramol and similar drugs follows a specific pattern, with the prefix Cosignifying combination. This naming system is widely used in the British National Formulary (BNF) for various combination drugs. These include antibiotics, gastrointestinal preparations, antihypertensives, diuretics, anti-Parkinsonian agents, and others. Additionally, this naming convention extends to medications used for treating migraines, such as Co-dergocrine and Co-careldopa, among others.
